newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil hovers around five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil hovers around five-year high.

text.p: Singapore gas oil rose to a new five-year high on strong buying interest bouyed by recent large Chinese and Indonesian purchases, traders said on Monday.

A trader was bidding for a 150,000-barrels second half December cargo at $31.90 per barrel, up 10 cents from its five-year traded high last week, with another buyer seen at $31.75 a barrel, both fob Singapore basis.

The market firmed on expectations of some new buying interest from players who had earlier sold December arrival cargoes to Indonesia. Indonesia had bought around 3.5 million barrels of gas oil for December arrival, traders said.

China has raised its gas oil purchases for December arrival by at least 100,000-tonnes. Chinese buyers paid a record $256-258 per tonne for small lots on an ex-termininal Hong Kong basis late last week.
The gas oil swaps market also picked up with December traded at $31.55, up about 10 cents from early day quotes, brokers said.

The jet fuel swaps market was offered down as traders looked to take profit on earlier sales. The December jet fuel/gas oil spread was down about 30 cents from Friday and was last traded at $1.35 a barrel, brokers said.
Naphtha was unchanged with little direction from crude or swaps. December paper was steady at $23.70/23.90 a barrel. Singapore refiners were quiet as their December barrels were already committed.

A Japanese trader offered two gasoline cargoes, selling one 50,000 barrels of 92-octane unleaded to a European major at $24.50 per barrel, fob, lifting end December. The second for 95-octane was offered down to $25.75 but failed to attract buyers. Bearish sentiment crept in on talks of half a million barrels of Thai 95-octane being offered lifting on January 1-15.
